newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Heavy casualties reported in combat near Bogota.
newsitem.headline: Heavy casualties reported in combat near Bogota.

text.p: Heavy fighting raged on Monday between troops and leftist rebels in a mountainous area 30 miles (50 km) east of Bogota amid unconfirmed reports that between 18 and 25 soldiers have been killed, authorities said.
The battle erupted Friday near San Juanito town, when about 50 soldiers of a counterinsurgency unit came under attack from Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas.

Armed forces chief Gen. Harold Bedoya said all radio contact with the troops had been lost since midday Sunday and it was impossible to give casualty details. But Bogota's El Tiempo newspaper said at least 18 soldiers had been killed in the attack and the TV Hoy news programme reported up to 25 dead.
Three helicopters ferrying reinforcements came under fire during the fighting and at least one airborne soldier was killed and two others were wounded, Bedoya said.
"We're facing an enemy that wants to destroy us and wants to destabilise society," Bedoya told reporters.

The fighting in San Juanito began shortly after the rebels released two kidnap victims, a Bogota businessman and French highway engineer Alain Fablet, seized by the FARC in October, military sources said.
Bedoya said on Monday that about 120 FARC rebels were involved in the attack.

In thinly veiled criticism of the failure of Colombia's civilian leaders to provide adequate materiel for the anti- guerrilla war, Bedoya told national radio: "We're at war with the narco-terrorists of the FARC and the National Liberation Army (ELN) but unfortunately (some sectors) have declared peace which means we don't have sufficient mechanisms to fight back."
Defence Minister Guillermo Alberto Gonzalez was unable to confirm the number of dead and injured in the weekend combat but said casualties could be high.

If reports of the number of dead are confirmed it would be the heaviest blow dealt to the army since the FARC overran a jungle base in southern Colombia last August, killing 27 soldiers and taking 60 prisoners.
